key_insight: In BiSBr, carrier localization is not intrinsic but is triggered extrinsically by vacancies that create defect-bound hot polarons and trap excited carriers before they reach the band edge.
engineering_relevance: This shows that controlling defect formation in pnictogen-based chalcohalides is essential for preserving mobile carriers and improving solar absorber performance.
method: Compared intrinsic carrier behavior with vacancy-induced defect effects
Analyzed hot-carrier coupling to defect-driven vibrational modes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that vacancies from synthesis or post-treatment produce above-gap defect states that divert hot carriers from cooling to the band edge, depleting the mobile carrier population.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend strongly on defect control during growth and post-treatment, so results may be sensitive to processing conditions and material purity.
paper_title: Carrier Localization in Pnictogen-Based Chalcohalides from Defect-Bound Hot Polarons
